mission: End-to-end test the consent architecture: grant -> capture eligibility -> withdrawal -> retroactive exclusion from training-eligible sets; ledger export integrity; version bumps.

dataset_scope.data: Synthetic-only. All fixtures generated in-test (SYNTHETIC-TEST-FIXTURE pseudonyms in package tests; PostgreSQL-generated UUID subjects in API integration tests). No user media, no held-out cases touched (wm-dink-01, afn-vic-rally1 untouched).
dataset_scope.database: Real PostgreSQL 16 via docker compose postgres_test (localhost:5433), full migrations 0001-0016 applied per isolated schema per test process.

configuration.new_contract: consent-ledger-export-v1 (versioned envelope: exportVersion, exportedAtIso, subjectPseudonym, recordCount, maxSeq, recordsSha256 over canonical record JSON, records[]). Legacy bare-array ledgers remain accepted by first-party intake for backward compatibility; envelope semantics were added as a new version, not softened in place.

findings_and_fixes.finding: No integrity-verifiable ledger export existed. The consent status endpoint's record shape (recordedAt) was incompatible with the first-party intake loader (recordedAtIso), and a bare-array export had no defense against tampering, truncation, reordering, record-count lies, or cross-subject record injection.
findings_and_fixes.fix: Added GET /v1/me/consent/export returning a consent-ledger-export-v1 envelope with sha256 over canonical records + seq monotonicity + maxSeq + recordCount + single-subject checks enforced by packages/first-party-intake/src/consentRef.ts. Export is audited (consent.ledger.exported) and pseudonymous (no user_id/email in payload).
findings_and_fixes.regression_tests: services/api/test/consent.e2e.integration.test.ts (tamper, truncation, reorder+count-lie, unknown version, foreign subject, pseudonymity+audit) and packages/first-party-intake/test/consentExport.test.ts (12 tests incl. empty-envelope default-deny, missing seq, wrong maxSeq, legacy array compat).

findings_and_fixes.finding: GDPR data export (POST /v1/me/export) omitted the first-party consent ledger entirely — a user's append-only consent history (grants AND withdrawals) was invisible in their own data export.
findings_and_fixes.fix: services/api/src/modules/privacy/routes.ts now joins consent_record via consent_subject and includes consentLedger in the export payload.
findings_and_fixes.regression_tests: consent.e2e.integration.test.ts: GDPR export contains all 4 ledger rows (2 grants, 1 v2 re-grant, 1 withdrawal) in seq order.

lifecycle_verified: Grant video_analysis + model_training -> dataset item training-eligible (1 item selected, grant_consent_version=model-training-v1)
Version bump: re-grant under model-training-v2 -> selection exposes ingest-time version v1 and authorizing grant version v2 separately (no silent relabel)
Withdrawal -> fresh selection returns 0 items; consent watermark advances
TOCTOU: stale pre-withdrawal selection re-verified via verifyTrainingEligibility on fresh connection returns 0 items
Withdrawal side effects: existing item removed_at set + ml_dataset_review deletion task queued; post-withdrawal item never eligible
Post-withdrawal export: trailing withdrawn record present; first-party intake denies model_training while video_analysis stays active (scopes independent)
Export before any ledger exists: typed 404 consent.no_ledger (missing consent = deny, no default grant)
